skill.name: vercel-deploy
skill.description: Guides deployment of Next.js applications to Vercel, including vercel.json settings, environment variables, custom domains, API rewrites, and troubleshooting.
skill.summary: Deploy and troubleshoot Next.js applications on Vercel.
skill.author: Awais68

security_audit.summary: The skill is mostly deployment documentation, and most static hits are false positives from Markdown code fences, placeholders, and configuration examples. Confirmed risks remain around production Vercel commands, local environment pulls, package installs, and API proxy examples that can forward authorization data.

remediation.issue: Environment pull command can write secrets to .env.local.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit approval before running `vercel env pull`, confirm `.env.local` is ignored, and avoid printing pulled values.

remediation.issue: Production deploy commands can change live infrastructure.
remediation.suggestion: Ask users to confirm the Vercel project, branch, and target environment before `vercel --prod` or token-based deploys.

remediation.issue: API proxy example forwards Authorization to an environment-derived upstream.
remediation.suggestion: Use a server-only upstream variable, validate allowed hosts, and forward authorization only to trusted services.

remediation.issue: CORS example allows every origin for API paths.
remediation.suggestion: Replace wildcard CORS with explicit production and preview origins, or document when wildcard access is safe.

semantic_findings.title: Overly Permissive API CORS Header
semantic_findings.description: The example sets Access-Control-Allow-Origin to `*` for API paths. Copying this into production can allow any origin to read API responses when other controls are weak.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The wildcard CORS header is explicitly present in the Vercel headers example. The risk depends on authentication and response sensitivity, so confidence is high but not absolute.

semantic_findings.title: Authorization Header Forwarded to Configured Upstream
semantic_findings.description: The Edge Function example forwards the incoming Authorization header to a URL built from NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL. A wrong upstream value could receive user bearer tokens.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The code sample shows a fetch to an environment-derived endpoint and forwards Authorization. It is a legitimate proxy pattern, but host validation is not shown.

content.value_statement: Vercel deployments fail when build settings, domains, and environment variables drift. This skill guides configuration, deployment, and troubleshooting for Next.js apps.
actual_capabilities: Drafts basic and advanced vercel.json settings for Next.js projects.
Explains Next.js configuration for images, redirects, headers, and standalone output.
Guides public and server-only environment variable setup for Vercel.
Provides Vercel CLI deployment, project linking, and CI command guidance.
Documents custom domain DNS records, redirects, and deployment troubleshooting steps.
Shows API rewrite and Edge Function patterns for backend proxying.
limitations: It is focused on Next.js projects deployed to Vercel.
It does not manage Vercel accounts, billing, or project permissions.
It cannot verify domains, secrets, or deployment status without user-provided access.
Its examples require review before use in regulated or high-risk production systems.

use_cases.title: Prepare a New Vercel Launch
use_cases.description: Create deployment settings, environment variable guidance, and a release checklist for a Next.js application.

use_cases.title: Standardize Deployment Configuration
use_cases.description: Document Vercel settings, custom domains, redirects, and cache headers for repeatable team deployments.

use_cases.title: Troubleshoot Failed Releases
use_cases.description: Review build errors, missing environment variables, domain records, and routing problems after a failed deployment.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Deployment Checklist
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a first Vercel release.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Vercel deployment checklist for my Next.js app. Include build settings, environment variables, domain setup, and final verification steps.

prompt_templates.title: Review Vercel Configuration
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate review of existing project settings.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my Vercel and Next.js deployment configuration. Identify missing settings, risky defaults, and changes needed before production.

prompt_templates.title: Plan API Rewrites
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced routing between frontend and backend services.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a safe Vercel API rewrite plan for my Next.js app. Include upstream URL handling, headers, CORS, and environment variable boundaries.

prompt_templates.title: Debug Production Deployment
prompt_templates.prompt: Help diagnose my failed Vercel production deployment. Check build commands, framework settings, environment variables, redirects, domains, and runtime errors.

output_examples.input: A developer asks for help preparing a Next.js app for first production deploy.
output_examples.output: A step-by-step deployment checklist covering build settings, public variables, server-only secrets, custom domain setup, and validation tasks.

output_examples.input: A team reports that API routes work locally but fail after deployment.
output_examples.output: A troubleshooting plan that checks rewrite targets, environment variable names, deployment logs, CORS settings, and backend availability.

output_examples.input: A release manager wants safer Vercel CI deployment guidance.
output_examples.output: A CI deployment review that separates preview and production releases, verifies token handling, and lists approval points before promotion.

best_practices: Use preview deployments before promoting changes to production.
Keep secrets server-only and confirm .env.local is ignored by source control.
Validate domains, redirects, and API rewrites against the real production architecture.
anti_patterns: Do not copy placeholder domains or tokens into production without replacement.
Do not expose database URLs, API secrets, or service tokens with NEXT_PUBLIC prefixes.
Do not deploy with production commands before confirming the target Vercel project.

faq.question: What projects is this skill for?
faq.answer: It is for Next.js applications that deploy to Vercel.

faq.question: Can it deploy backend-only applications?
faq.answer: No. It is not designed for backend-only services or non-Vercel hosting.

faq.question: Does it handle environment variables?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains public variables, server-only variables, and Vercel environment setup.

faq.question: Can it configure custom domains?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes DNS records, redirects, and Vercel domain setup guidance.

faq.question: Does it require Vercel CLI access?
faq.answer: Some workflows use the Vercel CLI, but dashboard-based setup is also described.

faq.question: Should production commands run automatically?
faq.answer: No. Production deploys and environment pulls should require explicit user approval.
